content: Jill Stein, a physician and activist affiliated with the Green-Rainbow Party, resides in Lexington, Massachusetts. She is a member of the boards of Greater Boston Physicians for Social Responsibility and MassVoters for Fair Elections. Additionally, she has been actively involved with the Massachusetts Coalition for Healthy Communities. In 2002, Jill Stein ran as the Green-Rainbow Party candidate for governor of Massachusetts. Her performance during the debates was widely praised; however, this did not translate into electoral success. She finished third out of five candidates, receiving 76,530 votes, which accounted for approximately 3.5% of the total vote. After her gubernatorial campaign, Stein ran for the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 2004, representing the Ninth Middlesex District. She was endorsed by State Representative Jay R. Kaufman. In the election, she secured 21.3% of the vote, placing ahead of Republican candidate Linda Fosburg, who received 18.9%. However, she was defeated by the Democratic incumbent, Thomas M. Stanley, who garnered 59.6% of the vote. In March 2005, Jill Stein was elected to a Town Meeting Seat in Precinct 2 of Northwest Waltham, Middlesex County, during the local elections. She finished first among 16 candidates competing for seven available seats, receiving 539 votes, which represented 20.6% of the total vote. On March 4, 2006, Jill Stein was nominated as the Green-Rainbow Party candidate for Secretary of the Commonwealth at the party's statewide nominating convention. She was the sole challenger to the three-term Democratic incumbent, Bill Galvin. The general election took place on November 7, 2006. In this head-to-head contest, Stein received 353,551 votes, which accounted for 18% of the total vote. This result marked the strongest performance by a Green Party candidate for Secretary of State in any U.S. state to date.
